findings.truth: L’Arroseur arrosé (1895), the gardener film described here, is a comic narrative rather than a simple actuality.
findings.evidence: Library of Congress, French and Francophone Film guide

findings.claim: the first commercially successful film apparatus
findings.truth: The Cinématographe combined camera, printer and projector functions and was patented in 1895, but the Kinetoscope was already being manufactured, sold and exhibited commercially in 1894.
findings.evidence: Library of Congress, Early Motion Picture Productions and Alice Guy-Blaché guide

findings.claim: By the early 1920s ... MGM, Paramount, Warner Bros., RKO and Fox ... came to dominate
findings.truth: The course timeline says the Big Five structure was established by 1930; RKO was formed in 1928.
findings.evidence: Eduqas specification, Appendix B; National Park Service RKO history

findings.claim: the first feature-length sound film to achieve mass commercial success
findings.truth: The Jazz Singer is largely silent, with synchronised music and vocal sequences. Its commercial impact helped drive the sound-film transition.
findings.evidence: Eduqas specification, Appendix B; AFI Catalog and MoMA entries for The Jazz Singer

findings.claim: Early critics complained that CinemaScope was only suited to ‘snakes and funerals’
findings.truth: The familiar remark is attributed to Fritz Lang in Contempt (1963), not to unnamed early critics.
findings.evidence: David Bordwell, CinemaScope chapter; fetched Los Angeles Times account

findings.claim: The Steadicam was invented by Garrett Brown in 1975
findings.truth: Garrett Brown created the Steadicam; the specification dates its first introduction to 1975. Its feature-film debut was Bound for Glory (1976).
findings.evidence: Eduqas specification, Appendix B; Tiffen History of Steadicam; American Cinematographer

findings.claim: streaming overtook DVD as the primary distribution or home-viewing format in 2017
findings.truth: The specified 2017 development is that online film and television services surpassed physical-disc sales in the United States.
Toy Story runs for 80–81 minutes; AFI lists 80–81 minutes and the Library of Congress lists 81 minutes.
findings.evidence: AFI Catalog; Library of Congress Toy Story screening record

findings.claim: partial sequences of mainstream releases from the early 2000s
findings.truth: The Dark Knight (2008) was the first major Hollywood film to include scenes shot with IMAX cameras.
findings.evidence: IMAX, Christopher Nolan’s Birthday Calls for a Celebration of his Work

findings.claim: The T-1000 sequence proves CGI could do something no physical effect could match, and its achievement is described as a first.
findings.truth: Options: retain this as a broad description of the effect, or revise it to say that CGI extended practical effects. Fetched production accounts document both practical and digital work, but do not establish the lesson’s undefined ‘first’ claim.
findings.evidence: American Cinematographer, Terminator 2: Judgment Day — For FX, The Future Is Now

findings.claim: exam questions specifically ask for Garrett Brown
findings.truth: Options: replace this promise with ‘Garrett Brown is named in the course timeline’, or retain it only if a verified current assessment supports it. The specification names Brown but does not promise question wording.
findings.evidence: Eduqas assessment section and Appendix B

findings.claim: exam questions specifically ask about the ‘first computer-generated feature’
findings.truth: Options: replace this promise with a course-scope reminder, or retain it only if a verified current assessment supports it. The specification identifies Toy Story but does not prescribe this question wording.
findings.evidence: Eduqas assessment section and Appendix B

findings.claim: the exam will test the distinction between IMAX presentation and IMAX capture
findings.truth: Options: remove the prediction while keeping the accurate distinction, or retain it only with verified current-assessment evidence. The specification identifies Avengers: Infinity War but does not promise this distinction as a question.
findings.evidence: Eduqas assessment section and Appendix B

findings.claim: Tangerine’s visual effects are presented as natural results of the iPhone’s own wide-angle lens
findings.truth: Options: describe the visual effect as an interpretation of the finished film, or attribute the set-up more fully to the iPhone, Moondog anamorphic adapters and a stabiliser. The fetched sources verify the equipment but not the lesson’s detailed aesthetic reading.

summary: Three lessons were checked. Nine verified factual corrections are supplied; five further claims need editorial adjudication rather than unsupported rewrites.
